## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph by boat.** My rating for boat salmon this week: **St. Joseph 3, South Haven 3, Grand Haven 1, Muskegon 1**.
- **St. Joseph:** troll small crankbaits in about 20-30 ft for coho, and try 50-60 ft for spring Chinook.
- **South Haven** is the close second: work 45-60 ft with small crankbaits and spoons, and fish spawn on the bottom.
- **Lures:** small crankbaits and small spoons in orange or green have been the consistent producers.
- **Skip Grand Haven and Muskegon** for boats unless new reports improve. Both had only slow-to-average boat fishing.

## Why

- **St. Joseph and South Haven are my picks because** the newest boat reports there were rated good (3), while Grand Haven and Muskegon were rated below average (1).
- **Small crankbaits and spoons are my lure picks because** they caught most fish at both good ports in the latest reports.
- **Depth ranges come from the reports, not from my own estimate.** The 20-30 ft and 45-60 ft ranges are where boats caught fish, so I'd expect that to be the right place to start.
- **I'd expect the picture to change quickly.** Early May water is warming and shifting, so I'd check the next report before committing.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest is Apr 30, six days old)**
- St. Joseph, Apr 30: coho on boats were "very good," with small crankbaits trolled in 20 to 30 ft working best. Boats also began catching spring Chinook in 50 to 60 ft (St. Joseph, 2025-04-30).
- South Haven, Apr 30: boats had "good fishing," with 45 to 60 ft the most productive. Small crankbaits and spoons caught most fish, and spawn on the bottom also worked (South Haven, 2025-04-30).
- Grand Haven, Apr 23 (no Apr 30 report): boat anglers in the near-shore river water caught "a few brown trout and coho," rated below average (Grand Haven, 2025-04-23).
- Muskegon, Apr 30: boat fishing was "hit or miss," with mixed bags and rated below average (Muskegon, 2025-04-30). The Apr 23 report also rated boats below average, with only an occasional coho on small spoons (Muskegon, 2025-04-23).

**Past seasons (history, not current conditions)**
- At similar water temperatures (about 47 F), St. Joseph boats did well on coho in 30 ft (St. Joseph, 2022-05-04), and St. Joseph boats did well on spoons in 80 ft in an earlier May (St. Joseph, 2023-05-10).
- Grand Haven and Muskegon boats had good early-May Chinook fishing in 25-70 ft in 2023 (Grand Haven, 2023-05-03; Muskegon, 2023-05-03). Those were different years, so I wouldn't rely on them over this year's reports.

**Conditions now (measured buoy temperatures)**
- Surface water for the week before May 6: St. Joseph 50 F (down 2 F), South Haven 47 F (down 7 F), Grand Haven 45 F (up 2 F), Muskegon 45 F (up 2 F) (buoy summary, 2025-05-06).
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension): a sharp drop in buoy surface temperature can signal upwelling, which can bring salmon toward piers and river mouths. South Haven's 7 F drop fits that pattern, but this is general guidance, not something a report said.
- Live modeled pierhead water and the wind forecast were not available in this check, so I can't say how the next few days' wind will affect boat trips.

## Caveats

- The newest report is from Apr 30, six days old, and there is no report yet for the week of May 7. Treat these ratings as a guide, not a live read.
- The water-temperature data is measured from offshore buoys, not modeled at the piers. The lake model and wind forecast were unavailable, so check the wind before launching.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon have no current boat reports beyond Apr 23 and Apr 30, so their ratings rest on thin, older data.
